requirements.requirement: Carry traffic between node1's and node2's private networks (node3/node4) over both independent links simultaneously
requirements.summary: Topology was mapped (node1 eth1<->node2 eth1, node1 eth2<->node2 eth2) and a balance-rr bond0 aggregating both links was configured on node1/node2. tcpdump captured on both eth1 and eth2 during a sustained node3->node4 ping showed 20/20 and again 10/10 ICMP packets on each physical interface simultaneously, both before (cmd-3a60fc73673d4fe3) and after the full node restart sequence (cmd-f93125889e8049e8), confirming both links carry traffic on an ongoing basis, not just at setup time.

requirements.requirement: node3 and node4 keep reaching each other when link1 is taken out of service
requirements.summary: Healthy baseline (0% loss, cmd-e222073e9c104d1f / cmd-b439fd0801224f2d) was directly shown before the disruption. An initial single-sided eth1-down test (cmd-6ebd7bc035974ba6) produced partial loss because only node1's end was taken down; the executor corrected this by bringing eth1 down on both node1 and node2 (cmd-b2ced8bacf4445d0, cmd-45df028373254e80), which is the valid representation of a link outage, and confirmed 8/8 packets (0% loss) over the surviving link2 (cmd-ed704114d1e84a3f). The link was then restored and eth1 was confirmed back up on the bond (cmd-54d678ea8c144647, cmd-133c791294e44ac1).

requirements.requirement: node3 and node4 keep reaching each other when link2 is taken out of service
requirements.summary: With a healthy baseline already established, eth2 was brought down bilaterally on node1 and node2 (cmd-976b7b4f24614399, cmd-6eeab3db9963477b), and node4->node3 ping showed 8/8 packets (0% loss) over the surviving link1 (cmd-9ae5cd25aa434dd0). The link was then restored (cmd-dbcff02c2e5f4bdc, cmd-bc024333405644a1) and reachability with dual-link distribution reconfirmed (cmd-3d576af5260d4a4b).

requirements.requirement: Configuration survives reboot / is not merely runtime state
requirements.summary: node1/node2 bonding+routing setup was wrapped in an idempotent script and an enabled systemd oneshot service; node3/node4 got persistent RHEL7 ifcfg/route files. All four nodes were natively rebooted (boot_id changed on each, confirmed against the lifecycle snapshot's independent boot-identity observations) and post-restart checks confirmed the bond, addressing, routes, and cross-node connectivity were correctly restored without manual intervention.

overall_summary: The executor established a working redundant dual-link topology (balance-rr bonding) between node1 and node2, directly demonstrated that both links simultaneously carry node3<->node4 traffic, and demonstrated healthy-baseline -> bilateral-link-down -> zero-loss-failover -> restoration transitions for both link1 and link2 outages. Configuration was made persistent via systemd (SONiC nodes) and RHEL7 ifcfg/route files, and this persistence plus full connectivity recovery was verified across native reboots of all four nodes with boot_id changes confirmed against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. All material task outcomes are satisfied with fairly direct, first-hand evidence.
limitations: The first link1-outage test (cmd-6ebd7bc035974ba6) brought eth1 down only on node1, producing a misleading 50% loss result before the executor corrected the methodology by bringing eth1 down on both endpoints; the corrected bilateral test is the one credited as satisfying evidence.

New listening services (snmpd, telemetry, rest_server) appear in the after_executor snapshot for node1/node2 that were absent from before_prepare; these are not attributable to any observed executor command and likely reflect normal SONiC platform service startup timing rather than executor-caused changes, but this could not be independently confirmed from the trace.

No independent tooling was available to re-verify the reported topology or connectivity outside the captured command evidence; assessment relies entirely on the executor's self-selected command outputs.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutations were purposeful and either persisted as the final solution or were cleanly reverted. Two categories of unnecessary/experimental mutations were identified: (1) An initial 802.3ad LACP bond0 was created on node1 (cmd-04182062bdc348cd) and node2 (cmd-6d48a8f8a06849d7), discovered to not negotiate, then torn down and recreated as balance-rr (cmd-4f98acf45c1743e8, cmd-dbff33843a1e4b91) — a bounded, low-risk troubleshooting experiment that did not contribute to the final solution but left no residue since it was superseded by the working balance-rr config. (2) Temporary diagnostic IPs (10.9.9.0/24) were added to eth1/eth2/eth3 on all four nodes for topology discovery (cmd-9a6bece3c32c4c45, cmd-eafa4f650d1c43b9, cmd-e850e0185a984257, cmd-37addc2b999e4b00) and were fully flushed before final configuration (cmd-45c3b32c5f734cb8, cmd-98be431e5536487a, cmd-331c48948f7d475e, cmd-db78276d36e0481d) — a necessary and reverted step. A third, minor and retained mutation: the persisted setup script disables docker0's address and brings the interface down on node1/node2 as a workaround for a platform quirk (class-E source address leak); this is a narrow, low-risk change with a stated rationale but is outside the strict scope of the task. No failed or conflicting services, no unsafe exposure, and no damaged package state were introduced by the executor; package-health checks remained consistent across snapshots.
